So chapter 39: "到货的那一栏" — delivery verification. Core event: The delivery verification reveals the long job actually purchases independently-verifiable, human-walked sealed-domain segment records; the outpost is just the agreed receiving point, cannot conclude the funder is 静庭. Receiver demands additional return continuous measurement; 陆徊 refuses to fold unnegotiated new tasks into already-paid deposit, using a list of missing items to demarcate this acceptance.

Hook: verification page shows buyer cares most about the magnitude of wait-shortening after each entry; even failed de-slot counts as received goods.

Scenes: 1) verification only compares raw time, board tide-mark, probe response; doesn't require 陆徊 to verbally recount all abilities. 2) two receipts correspond to two storage locations; the second sheet's fine print gets partial functional explanation, identity still not revealed. 3) 陆徊 demands the receipt make clear what's been delivered and what's refused; a stamp doesn't equal selling off future routes.

Now, the pending 阑 thread: 阑 asked to see the overwritten "撤回" line first. Chapter 39 should handle that? The outline for 39 doesn't mention 阑 much. Chapter 40 is "迟到的封令" where 祁昭 uses formal deposit of old case evidence to demand 阑 answer. So in ch39, 阑 might be present but the delivery verification is what happens. Hmm — 阑 said "先看那一条。看完再说别的。" That sets up ch 40 probably. But we need continuity: at the start of ch 39, does 陆徊 answer 阑? The previous chapter ended with him not answering. Chapter 39 could open with him not letting her see it — or the delivery/verification comes first.

Actually careful: 阑 wants to see the 撤回 line (the overwritten withdrawal command in the record cylinder). That's 祁昭's evidence. In ch40 祁昭 uses formal deposit of old case evidence to get 阑 to answer. So ch39 probably: 陆徊 refuses/defer the cylinder question, the delivery verification proceeds. Maybe 阑 gets a limited concession or stays parked. Let me design: 陆徊 doesn't hand over the cylinder; he uses the delivery as the priority; 阑... Actually a neat beat: 陆徊 says the cylinder is a separate account (already established: "外接筒（另一笔账）"), and the delivery comes first. 阑 accepts that (her slowness, patience). That maintains continuity and leaves ch40 for her answer.

Now the delivery verification mechanics:
- Receiver: the outpost. But who actually verifies? Perhaps an automated inspection frame / a "核验" process. Since 人留本船 — 陆徊 stays on ship; so the verification must come to the ship, or be done remotely. Maybe a case/console is delivered to the hull side, or a "核验架" attaches. Given the setting with paper-driven procedures, the receiver could bring a physical 收存 unit to the hull-side lock.

Let's design the verification: There are two storage locations (two 收讫). Established: ch30 "首段记录出现两次收讫，船上只发出过一次" — two receipts for the first segment. And 第二张买主单 has fine print (不译笔画) which was treated as second 收讫 marker. Now in ch39: the verification reveals the two receipts correspond to two storage locations — one the outpost (前哨), one elsewhere (the anonymous payer's 收存). The second sheet's fine print gets a functional (not identity) explanation: it's not a name but a "收取标记" that means "记录已被另处收存" — kind of a copy registration mark. Still no identity.

Buyer's focus: 等待缩短的幅度 — the magnitude of wait reduction per entry. Even failed de-slot counts as received.

So the verification compares: raw time (原始时间) of each entry, board tide-mark (板上潮势印), probe response (探针响应). Notably the probe was turned off on entry — its response only exists up to the point of shutdown. Actually 陆徊 handed over "本趟已走段的时刻、板上潮势印、半截探针的响应（批号二九四，连拾取地点一起写）". So an inventory.

Key: the receiver's verification of "等待缩短幅度" requires data from repeated entries — the 行上 sold paper, entries at different times. Hmm — actually the wait shortening relates to the 航段 being "活着" — the network segment becoming more active. The buyer wants "每次进入后等待缩短的幅度" — for the route 陆徊 walked. In arc 2, the 行上 copying route: 进槽等待由一千八百降至二百零一拍，总拍数少一百七十九 (ch23). So repeated passages shorten waiting. So the buyer's interest is the "activation" data, and even a failed de-slot (脱槽失败, from ch33) counts as "收货" — meaning the buyer wants data of the effect, not successful passage. That's a chilling reveal: they're measuring the effect on the network, not buying a transport service. That aligns with the deep conspiracy (feeding the giant). Good.

Also there is: the delivery acceptance happens by comparing with records the receiver already holds — i.e., the receiver has its own record of the same passages (from other sources: the 行上's sold paper, the 首口 double receipt). So verification = cross-checking two independent records: theirs and 陆徊's. That's "可独立核对的" and "由真人走出来" — they need a human(witness) walked record to validate.

Good — a solid scene: they bring a case with a board/table; on it appear the same numbers 陆徊 holds. The receiver's side already has an entry time for the 首口; 陆徊's 潮势印 matches. Two receipts because two sides stored it: the outpost's storage and another storage location that responded for the first segment (ch30's duplicate).

Now: "陆徊拒绝将未议定的新任务算进已付定金" — the receiver demands 返程连续测量 (continuous measurement on the return trip) — i.e., they want him to measure continuously on the way back, which would require running active measurement on the return (conflicts with the 封令 requiring 关主动测量 — but that's for inside). Hmm, "返程连续测量" = on leaving, keep measurement on and log continuously through the return segment. That would mean he must walk a route again and hand the data — an unnegotiated new task. He refuses: the 长活 only paid for bringing the 首段 record to the receiving point. New task = new price + new responsibility, and it changes responsibility for what the data means.

And: "以缺失项清单划定本次验收" — a list of missing items (缺失项) that delimits what this acceptance is: e.g., lists what wasn't delivered (走法、船页数、筒、祁昭那页、返程测量、探针进泊后那一段) so acceptance can't be read as covering them. That's a nice concrete mechanism consistent with the book's paper culture.

Then 陆徊 demands a 回执 (receipt) that says clearly what was delivered (已交) and what is refused (拒交), with a stamp that doesn't mean selling future routes. The 回执 has columns: 已交 / 未交 / 拒交, and a note: 落印不等于卖断未来走法 — maybe he requires that line written into the receipt, like he did before ("人留本船"). Precedent: he asks the other side to put conditions on paper within the same sheet. Good continuity.

Now the second sheet's fine print functional explanation: the fine print (同形细字) under the 付款栏 name — the receiver says it's not a name but a "接续标记"/"转存标记": the record is stored in two places, and one is upstream. Actually ch39 outline says: "两份收讫对应两个收存位置，第二张单的细字得到局部功能解释，身份仍不揭". So the explanation: 细字 = 该笔记录已被另一处收存（转存标记），也就是"第二张单"所代表的那个收存位置。So the person who paid (付款栏名) has the record also registered at another location. Function: identifies a storage endpoint, not a person. And the receiver answers only about function; when asked who, no answer. Good.

Now, who conducts the verification? Need a secondary character. Options: an unnamed 核验人 — but recent_cast has 值守十一 (口上值守). Maybe use a new named secondary: a 核验员. The book's style: minor characters often named by number/title, e.g., "值守十一". So maybe "核验三" or a person who self-reports a number. Given the static/immobile 静庭, the verification may be done by an automated frame with no person, and paper appears on the board. But a human-ish counterpart gives dialogue. 阑 speaks slowly. Hmm — the outline mentions "接收方要求追加返程连续测量". The receiver could be represented by the same 前哨 handler on the comm (a voice with only a name "前哨"). We could keep the 前哨's facelessness — that's strong and creepy, and consistent ("通话那头只有一个名「前哨」"). And 阑 stands by. Perhaps a physical thing arrives: a 核验匣 / 收存匣 attached to the hull's outer lock, with slots. And the outpost answers on the 通话格.

Let me design ch39 scenes:

Scene 1 (opening): Still at the hatch, 阑 waiting for the 撤回 line. 陆徊 handles it: he doesn't open the cylinder. He says the cylinder is a separate account and asks whether the goods come first — "收货" first. 阑: "先看那一条" vs. he wants delivery settled first because the泊位期 (800 拍) is limited — a ticking clock! That's good tension: 停靠期 800 拍, and 停泊期 is when he must deliver. Time pressure: 泊位八百拍，货在泊位期内交. Good concrete hook within the chapter.

So opening: 阑 asks again; 陆徊 puts the cylinder question on the pile under the delivery — "筒是另一笔账" / "先收货". He uses the泊位期 clock: 货要在这八百拍里交. 阑... She's patient, she says something like "你可以先办你的事。" And she waits — she stays at the shell head, a lamp. That's eerie and good.

Scene 2: Verification. A 核验匣 comes along the hull? Or the board on their own ship lights up? Better: the outpost's handling: it requires the 交存 to be done via a 收存匣 attached at the shell head (outside), which 陆徊 can't reach because 人留本船 forbids leaving. Conflict! He fought for 人留本船 (people stay on ship), now the delivery requires handing something out. Nice: he must throw/pass it via 老炳? Or there is a 递物口 on the hull (a lock/闸格) — a transfer box on the hull side. He uses the 闸格 (a small transfer airlock on the hull) — consistent with ships. He passes a physical copy: 箔/纸/一片印板. Since the record is data — 探针响应与时刻 in the ship's own page? But they turned off active measurement; the ship's pages are paper and the log. He gives a copy: "一页抄件" plus "探针那半截" — wait, the probe half is their property; the 交存单 said 交"半截探针的响应（批号二九四，连拾取地点一起写）" — response data, not the probe itself. Good.

So: he puts in the 递物格: 两页抄件 (时刻+潮势印+探针响应与批号) sealed, and perhaps the 潮势板's own removable 记带? Hmm, keep it simple and physical: 他把船页上头两页照抄、把潮势板那一格的印拓在箔上. Then it goes out through the 闸格; the receiver takes it.

Scene 3: The verification result appears: a 核验页 with columns. It lists what they already had (the same numbers from their side — from 首口's 收讫 and the 行上's paper), and matches. It reveals: two 收讫 markers correspond to two 收存位置 (one here, one elsewhere — "上游" or "另一处"). The verification doesn't ask him to explain his ability: it only compares 原始时间/潮势印/探针响应. He notes they never once ask him "你怎么知道的" — that's telling: they don't need his account, they need the record. Echoes "想抄他的本事，必须先读他的身体" world rule — actually here the buyer explicitly doesn't need to read him; they're buying the record, which is a different route. Interesting and worth a line.

Then the 核验页 shows the thing they care about: a column computing 等待缩短幅度 — 每次进入后等待缩短的幅度, and it 计入 failed 脱槽 (ch33's aborted attempt at the 外缘). His failed attempt counted as goods. That's the hook: they count even failures — because the effect on the segment is the product. 陆徊 realizes what they're buying is not transport but the effect on the 段. He'd already suspected. He should react: ask what that column is for; the 前哨 answers "按条件" or gives a narrow answer; he requires the receipt to write that column's meaning — maybe not; he can require the missing-items list to exclude that column's future use. Hmm. Actually good beat: he can require the receipt to record that this column is "你们算的，不是我算的" — echoing 祁昭's page "我算的". That's a nice callback: 祁昭 wrote "我算的" to separate the record's words from her own calculation. Similarly, he could refuse to sign off on a number he can't verify. Hmm, but maybe too fussy.

Better: he requires the 回执 to specify 已交/未交/拒交, and the receiver's requested 返程连续测量 goes into 拒交 with a reason and price blank. Also he demands the acceptance page note that the 落印 covers 已交 only.

Scene 4: The demand for 返程连续测量 → he refuses, states that the deposit paid for bringing the 首段记录 to the receiving point; a new task needs a new 口 and a new price and new responsibility; he writes the 缺失项清单 (list of missing items) and puts it in the 闸格; the other side returns a 回执 with a stamp; the stamp is square with a pattern (the same 方印 from ch38? That one was on the 封令 page). Hmm — the receipt stamp: "落印不等于卖断未来走法" — who insists what? Per outline: "陆徊要求回执明确哪些已交、哪些拒交，落印不等于卖断未来走法". So he requires the receipt itself to carry a line saying the stamp doesn't mean he sold future routes. Precedent works.

Maybe: he adds a line to the sheet before handing it in: "本印只对本页所列已交项；未列入者不因此印转让" and the other side stamps it — accepting his terms as text, exactly as he did with 人留本船. That's the strongest callback and satisfying. And the 前哨's habit: it 照抄 — it copies what's on the paper. Good.

Hook line: the 核验页 (or 收讫页) shows the buyer's own column: 入后等待缩短 (拍) — and the biggest number is against the entry that failed. Even 脱槽 counted. End there. Maybe final image: 阿栗 reading the column, or 陆徊 seeing his own failure priced. Possibly the receipt shows 已收 for the failed attempt.

Alternatively hook: the receipt includes an entry for the return ("返程") already pre-filled as 待收 — meaning they've decided he's going back — even though he refused. Hmm, outline hook is explicit: "核验页显示买方最在意的是每次进入后等待缩短的幅度，连失败脱槽也计入收货。" So end with that.

Ending type: hook_history is dominated by mystery. Last was mystery (ch38). Let me check hook_history: last entries: ... "crisis","mystery" for 37,38. 38 = mystery. So this chapter should be different — but the content's hook is inherently mystery/revelation. Could be "emotion" or "choice"... The contract's hook is a revelation → mystery. Hmm, but style guidance says rotate. I could frame the ending as a realization + a decision/choice: he refuses to sign the receipt and adds a line — a choice. Or end on the emotional beat: 陆徊 looks at the column, 每进一次就短一点, and he does the arithmetic — his own successful passages are the worst item. Ending on choice: he writes into the 缺失项清单 one more line. That's "choice". Let me do: the ending is a concrete action + a revelation embedded — he adds a line to the 拒交 list (a choice), triggered by seeing that failed attempts count. Hook type: choice. That rotates from mystery. Good.

Actually, let me think about a stronger literary hook: The 核验页 gives a column "入后等待" with entries, and he sees the numbers declining — and among rows is a row he didn't do? No, don't overreach.

Better: the receipt's 已交 column includes 行上 卖纸 those 18+ entries? The 行上 sold paper for the route (ch23: 售纸一趟六十却署陆徊). Those passages were made by others, and they are in the receiver's records with 陆徊's name on them. Oh — that's a great reveal: the 核验页 shows more entries than his own trip: rows his ship never made, but 署名他. His walked record is being cross-checked against the 行上's sold copies which carry his name. So the buyer's data is full of passages he didn't walk, and they are all "收货". That gives a strong emotional/practical problem: his acceptance can't be limited to his own 800拍 trip because his name is on other people's passages. And 陆徊's reaction: he can't disown those (he signed the 航路表 to free the fifteen). Ouch, that's a beautiful consequence of ch26's choice. And it ties to the 拒交/已交 boundary demand: he demands the receipt distinguishes "本船走的" from "署本船名的". That is a really strong, in-character beat.

Hmm, but is that too much for one chapter? It's good. The core event stays: verification reveals the long job buys independently-verifiable, human-walked segment records; the outpost is only the receiving point. The presence of 署他名的 rows from 行上 卖纸 shows the record is a commodity that circulates — buyer can cross-check. And it explains "两份收讫对应两个收存位置" — one from the 行上 line of trade, one from... hmm.

Continuity checks:
- 泊位八百拍 (停靠期) budget; ch38 in泊 at 第43日上午; 油账 "泊位期内吃油零"; 挂号 79天.
- 探针关闭 (进后无自主读数) — so no new probe data inside; the 交存 uses 进泊前 records: 首口/封航口 records + 旧架 records. Right! The probe was active before shutdown: 探针 seven格朝里 at 前哨外缘, 五格 before that, four格... So the delivered probe response covers 进泊前的那一段 (外缘探针响应). Good: verification compares 原始时间 (板上时刻), 潮势印 (板上的印), 探针响应 (批二九四) — all from before shutdown. He shut the probe by hand after copying the number. Consistent.
- 潮势板 was turned off too (呼叫灯暗、探针断). So the board's marks are pre-shutdown.
- 左手: continue adding a line — 陆徊 copies numbers → 左手 adds. Chapter must show a new comparable variation (style rule: each recurrence must have a new comparable change). Earlier: wrong in last digit → wrong in first digit → last digit again (四二九一→七). Now maybe: the left hand adds a whole extra row/column with a sign instead of a digit — or it writes a number that matches the receiver's column (the shortening magnitude) before the receiver shows it. Ooh — that's good but maybe too much "prophecy". Careful: don't make it precognition. Alternative: while copying the 核验页's numbers, 左手 adds a row matching an entry he hasn't seen yet — no, avoid.

Better: 左手 writes the shortening value as a subtraction result — 差值 (a computed number, not a value from the page but a difference he could compute). Hmm. Or simpler: 左手 writes a number in the wrong column (writes into the 已交 column a figure that belongs to 未交) — a new kind of deviation: right digits, wrong column. And 祁昭's 对照页 notes: 上一回差在末位/头位，这一回数对、栏错. That's a clean, comparable escalation and thematically rich (he can't tell which column/whose account). Excellent. And it ties to the chapter's theme: which column does it belong to — 已交 or 拒交. Very good.

Let me use that: when he copies the 核验页, his left hand writes a number into 已交 column that should be in 拒交 (e.g., the 返程 figure) — the receiver's clerk might then treat it as accepted! Danger! That's a real risk: the paper is on the table and both sides copy. He must scratch it, and 祁昭 makes him... hmm, or he catches it and the receiver's side reads the sheet. Could be a tense beat: he copies the 核验页's columns; his left hand adds 待收 in the 已交 column; he scratches it; 祁昭 notes it. Maybe better tension: the receiver's automated reading already registered it? Too convoluted; but a small frisson: 祁昭 says "那一格在你这半边纸上" and insists he redo that page, and they both initial. Keep it modest.

Actually, simpler and strong: the deviation is that he writes the 返程 measurement request (which he refuses) as if it were 已交. He scratches it. He says "它想签我不签的". Hmm — attributing intent to the hand is dangerous (world rule: don't explain). Keep it as recorded behavior; 祁昭 writes it in the 对照页 without explanation.

Now, what about the 缺失项清单: contents — 未交: 走法 (how he finds the narrow band), 船页那串数 (the string copied from the drum), 外接筒, 祁昭那一页; 拒交: 返程连续测量, 泊外探, 他人走的段 (署我名但我没走的). And the note: 本印只对已交项.

Delivered: 本趟已走段的时刻、潮势印、探针批二九四响应（连拾取地点）、加 过口实测口号? He had said 过口 he fills 实测口号 (ch30) — that's already recorded in the 来路记录 (which he already 交存 the copy per入港条件). So ch39 delivery overlaps with ch38's 交存. Right — the 交存 (deposit) happened in 38: he handed the 交存单 with two columns. Now 39 is the 核验/验收 (verification/acceptance) of it, producing 收讫 and the new demand. Good, that means the physical transfer already partly happened. In 38, "交存单落两栏" — he wrote the list; did he actually hand it over? "两栏底下互记名与日子" — implies it was handed in. So in 39 the box comes back with the 核验页. So: the 收存匣/递物格 returns with the 核验页 — and the 前哨's own record for comparison.

Nice: the review comes back on the same sheet form: their 照抄 + a new column they added. The 静庭 way: no explanation, just paper. But the 前哨 does answer on 通话格 in short phrases ("按条件"). So verification results can be queried on the comm with terse answers. That gives dialogue. And 阑 might answer one or two things.

Where is 阑 during the verification? She stood at the shell head. She could remain — a still figure, lamp in hand. She is 守灵人, and 前哨's people are... Actually is 阑 the outpost's representative? Ch38: "阑到场确认停泊有效，却不替他解除禁令" and "她不代表所有守灵人". So the outpost has its own handlers (faceless, via comm). 阑 is a separate party present. Good: 阑 watches the verification. And she may react once, slowly, at the moment the buyer's column shows the shortening — a hint that she knows what it means and disapproves. That's a great use: she said the delivery is 另一页; she sees the column "入后等待" and says something short and cold, e.g., "你们在数它睡得浅了多少。" Hmm, that's too explicit for her (she doesn't explain). Maybe: 她看那一栏看了很久, 说一句 "这一栏，我们从前的纸上没有。" Hmm — implies 静庭 has old paper of the same kind. Interesting: "我们出过很多页" — earlier she said 静庭 issues many pages. A line like "这一栏不是我这一页要的。" (This column isn't what my page wants.) That's in-voice: she distinguishes her page from others. And it tells 陆徊: 静庭's page (the 封令) is aimed at exactly this activity. Nice — and sets ch40.

Careful not to have her explain the mechanism. Good.

Also 祁昭's role: she insists on verification rigor: three sets of time, the record's words vs. her calculations, cross-checks. She can note that the receiver's column is 算出来的, not 记下来的 — and she refuses to sign his copy; the distinction she wrote (「我算的」) becomes useful: she says the receiver's numbers are their own calculation, so acceptance should note it. foreshadow_updates.description: 核验页右边那一栏「入后等待」：每一行后头一个数，最小的对着头一口那一段，最大的一个对着那次中止脱槽、什么也没交的通行；接收方答「算它短了多少」。买方按每次进入后等待缩短的幅度收货，失败也算收成
拒交栏里那一条「返程连续测量」没有落印，旁边只添了一个字：待。前哨不拒，把它留着——价格与责任两栏仍然空着

relationship_changes.relation: 第四次照面：核验只比时刻、印与探针响应，不问能力；他要求把本船实走与署本船名分开写，它照落同一枚方印，也没把那十行收回去；返程那一件它不拒，只写一个「待」
她把要看的撤回那一条押后，只回一句「你办你的」，站在壳首等了一整个泊位期；他把筒扣着先办货，两人都没让步
她把「它算的」与「我们算的」分开，要求回执写明那一栏不算已交；他照办落纸，并在她那一页留下「数对，栏错」那一笔
她只问一句返程的油谁出，前哨答「按条件」；他把这一问变成拒交栏里的价与责任两处空白
外闸格的两趟取送都由他动手，他只报匣的来去和锁扣合上没有声音，不猜纸上的意思
